review: Frozen four-module mate-free full-star contraction component
summary: The four frozen modules construct actual mate-free selected stars under an explicit small-left upper-degree premise, then contract the entire original host using selected stars and residual singleton branches. The quotient is a genuine simple graph with a covering, bounded MinorModel, original-host mate-free branches, the stated real boundary budget and exact vertex loss. No semantic defect found in this bounded component review. This is not a proof of the printed minimum-only Lemma 4.2, a cleaning theorem, a density increment, or a whole-paper certification.

source_reference.correspondence: The argument implements mate-edge augmentation and transfer back to the original graph for the explicitly small-left domain. It does not use the printed inference from a left minimum degree to the required upper degree. For ell>=1 and nonempty A, selected center-plus-leaf branches give a nonempty source-style mate-free induced-star family. Since selected leaves lie in A and centers in B, B minus C equals B outside the selected branch union.
source_reference.unmated_convention: The formal Unmated filter ranges over all w in the finite host, without a w != v condition. It counts v itself when degree(v) >= eps2*d. Added mate edges require x != y, and MateFreeOn likewise constrains only distinct vertices. This asymmetry is correctly used as an upper bound: augmented left neighbors are a subset of the diagonal-inclusive mate filter. No equivalence with a convention excluding self-mates is asserted. The prior small-dense/unmated alternative supplies this exact stronger filter predicate.

exact_endpoint.name: MinorFreeSpanners.unmated_small_left_full_star_contraction
inputs: Finite vertex type V with DecidableEq, actual SimpleGraph G, and finite side sets A and B with G.IsBipartiteWith A B
Natural ell and d, with d > 0; real K, eps1 and eps2 with 0 <= eps1 < 1 and eps2 > 0
For every x in A, actual original-host degree(x) <= K*d and at least d actual B-neighbors
The actual existing diagonal-inclusive Unmated G K eps1 eps2 d predicate
outputs: C subset B and a finite leaf assignment L supported on C, with actual original-host center-leaf adjacency, leaf independence and pairwise disjoint leaf sets
Exactly ell leaves at each selected center
Every selected leaf has at most eps1*d actual original-host neighbors in B minus C
C is nonempty if A is nonempty
A MinorModel of the explicit fullStarContraction G C L in the same original host G
Each minor branch has at most ell+1 vertices and is MateFreeOn G (eps2*d)
Every original host vertex belongs to a branch

findings.detail: Adjacency is literally old G adjacency OR a distinct pair inside A whose original G common-neighbor count reaches q. Symmetry uses original common-neighbor symmetry; distinctness suppresses added loops. Every old edge remains, and every edge incident to a vertex outside A is unchanged. Bipartiteness excludes old A-A edges, so each augmented left neighbor lies in the actual mate filter. A selected center lies in B and hence outside A; its augmented center-leaf edges are original G edges. Independence transfers to G by old-edge inclusion and excludes every distinct same-star pair meeting the original mate threshold. Opposite-side center-leaf common-neighbor sets are empty; q>0 supplies strict mate-freeness for these pairs.

The integer theorem internally selects full independent stars in the augmented graph using the actual left-degree and B-neighbor bounds; the previously proved maximum-packing selection is called with no new oracle. Transfer returns the same C and L to original G and the boundary estimate is justified by actual edge inclusion. The real specialization explicitly applies Unmated only after furnishing hsmall for each A vertex. For t=eps1*d, hd and he1 establish t>=0, and eps1<1 yields floor_nat(t)<d. A strict real mate-count bound is safely weakened to <=t and then to count<=floor_nat(t). The final original-host boundary count is cast to real and bounded by floor_nat(t)<=t. No ceiling, negative-floor assumption or nonintegral degree threshold is silently substituted.

The vertex type is a disjoint sum of actual selected-center labels and every actual vertex outside the entire center-plus-leaf union. Branches are precisely selected stars or residual singletons. Coverage follows by membership in that union or its complement. Disjointness checks star-star via A/C disjointness and original leaf disjointness, both star/residual orientations via complement membership, and residual-residual via distinct singleton labels. Every selected branch is connected by original G walks through its center; residual singletons use nil walks. Quotient adjacency requires distinct labels and an actual crossing G edge, so loops disappear and multiple crossing witnesses give one proposition-valued edge. Its MinorModel uses these exact branches and crossings. Width follows from actual leaf capacity plus one center; singletons fit ell+1. Mate-freeness uses the selected-star result or vacuity for singletons. The selected union has exactly (ell+1)*|C| vertices; its size is <=|V|, explicitly preventing truncated-natural-subtraction errors. Residual size is the exact complement cardinality, yielding |quotient|+ell*|C|=|V|.

The endpoint obtains C, L, fullness, mate-freeness, the boundary bound and conditional nonemptiness from the actual original-host selection. Bipartite side disjointness and C subset B supply Disjoint A C. It then returns the explicit fullMinorModel for these exact G, C and L, with boundedness, mate-freeness, coverage and exact cardinality from the corresponding construction. There is no replacement graph, unrelated minor witness or hidden cleaning/density premise.

issues.detail: This proves the small-left/regularized specialization, not printed minimum-only Lemma 4.2. The upper-degree premise must remain visible in downstream claims. Regularization and a reapplied actual small-dense/unmated alternative are separate prior results; deletion-invariance of Unmated is not assumed.

Unmated does not exclude w=v, whereas added edges and MateFreeOn exclude equal endpoints. The construction is valid for that exact predicate. Do not silently replace it with a weaker distinct-other-vertices predicate or claim their equivalence.

domain_and_scope_notes: Mathlib IsBipartiteWith requires disjoint sides and every edge crossing between them; it does not require A union B = V. Any vertices outside both sides are isolated and are retained as residual singletons.

No positive K assumption is needed for the actual endpoint: the explicitly supplied small-left degree bounds and minimum-neighbor bounds enforce what is necessary when A is nonempty. The source application has K>=ell>=1.

ell=0 is a valid extension: selected stars and residual branches are singletons, the boundary claim over selected leaves is vacuous and the exact vertex loss is zero. Nontrivial source claws use ell>=1.
A empty is allowed; nonemptiness is correctly conditional. If ell>=1, the size condition forces B empty. The full contraction still retains every host vertex.
eps1=0 and nonempty A cannot satisfy the strict Unmated hypothesis on those explicitly small A vertices; this is a permitted vacuous boundary case, not a rounding defect.
The full quotient contains every crossing original edge by definition; no quantitative estimate on edges lost inside branches or merged between branches is proved.
Only the selected leaf vertices receive the stated B-minus-C boundary budget. It is not a statement about every host vertex, every center, or every residual vertex.
The output is an explicit branch family and simple quotient minor. No separate forest-valued F packaging or completed source clean-claw theorem is asserted.
